content.glance: BNS s. 186 — Prohibition of fictitious stamps.

sections.heading: The legal rule
sections.body:
186. (1) Whoever—
(a) makes, knowingly utters, deals in or sells any fictitious stamp, or knowingly uses for any postal purpose any fictitious stamp; or
(b) has in his possession, without lawful excuse, any fictitious stamp; or
(c) makes or, without lawful excuse, has in his possession any die, plate, instrument or materials for making any fictitious stamp,
shall be punished with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees
(2) Any such stamp, die, plate, instrument or materials in the possession of any person for making any fictitious stamp may be seized and, if seized shall be forfeited
(3) In this section “fictitious stamp” means any stamp falsely purporting to be issued by Government for the purpose of denoting a rate of postage, or any facsimile or imitation or representation, whether on paper or otherwise, of any stamp issued by Government for that purpose
(4) In this section and also in sections 178 to 181 (both inclusive), and sections 183 to 185 (both inclusive) the word “Government”, when used in connection with, or in reference to any stamp issued for the purpose of denoting a rate of postage, shall, notwithstanding anything in clause (12) of section 2, be deemed to include the person or persons authorised by law to administer executive Government in any part of India or in any foreign country

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 186 constitutes a key component of Chapter X (Of Offences Relating to Coin, Currency-Notes, Bank-Notes, and Government Stamps) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, addressing prohibition of fictitious stamps. The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. The prosecution must establish every statutory element beyond reasonable doubt: the specified actus reus, the requisite mens rea, and any relevant statutory circumstances. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. Where statutory exceptions or provisos are attached to the section, the accused must establish facts bringing the case within such provisions under evidentiary standards.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of prohibition of fictitious stamps under Section 186 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 186.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 186 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 186 vs General Attempt: Section 186 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter X; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.

Section 186 vs Cognate Chapter Offences: Liability under Section 186 is distinguished by its specific mental threshold and the particular legal interest protected under Of Offences Relating to Coin, Currency-Notes, Bank-Notes, and Government Stamps.

Rule: Under BNS s. 186, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 186.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 186 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
